**Is 'opposite' a property of the names? (iteration-9 correction)** Each of the 300 forced prompts names its algorithm by one of three aliases, and the aliases of the edge algorithms share words with the banned names. On iteration 8's own stored geodesics at block 31 (every gate passes: the stored labels, prompt groups and algorithm-level g reproduce to 1e-9, and an independent kNN-geodesic recomputation from the stored states correlates with the stored k 15 matrix at 1.000), each non-banned algorithm was split into its three alias sets of 10 prompts and each set's g was computed (unit-weight Dijkstra 18.1 to 24.2, jump point search 14.2 to 18.8, IDA* 11.8 to 15.6, bidirectional A* 11.0 to 12.3, bidirectional BFS 9.2 to 12.4). The lexical overlap was committed by hash before any alias-level number: the number of banned-name detectors an alias matches (0 for every unit-weight Dijkstra and jump point search alias, 1 for every bidirectional BFS and bidirectional A* alias, 1 to 3 for IDA*). Across the 15 alias sets at k 15 the Spearman correlation is -0.61 (exact one-sided p 0.009 over all 360,360 assignments; 95% interval over template resamples -0.71 to -0.59), -0.77 at k 10 (p 0.0007), and -0.77 with content-word overlap. That statistic treats the 15 sets as exchangeable although they are nested in five algorithms, and between algorithms lexical overlap is confounded with mechanism: bidirectional BFS is next to BFS both in name and in mechanism. At the level of algorithms the correlation is -0.63 with p 0.13 (exact over 120 permutations; the tied overlap vector cannot go below 0.033). By the committed wording rule: g follows alias overlap across algorithms (rho -0.61, exact p 0.009), but the pattern is carried by algorithm identity; on this manifold names and mechanisms are confounded, and TP-G's name-free manifolds decide.
